label: rem:speed-of-light-regimes-lieb-robinson
title: Regime behaviour and Lieb--Robinson decay for $c_q$
html:
The speed of light c_q = 1/(q-1) (speed of light) is a derived, q-dependent quantity. This remark records the q-connection decomposition that produces it, its regime behaviour, the Lieb--Robinson decay of the causal cone, and its place among the information-theoretic speed limits.

The q-connection decomposition. The archimedean q-connection (q-connection) splits the gauge potential into horizontal (spatial) and vertical (Reeb/temporal) components:

  A_q =  q^{-1}A
  +  (1 - q^{-1})\iota_\xi A\varTheta
  =  q^{-1}A
  +  \hbar_q\iota_\xi A\varTheta.

The weight q^{-1} controls horizontal information transfer (spatial propagation between fibres), while \hbar_q = 1 - q^{-1} controls vertical information processing (Reeb flow within a fibre). Each f_q-iteration applies A_q once, simultaneously advancing the Reeb phase by \hbar_q and correlating adjacent fibres with coupling strength q^{-1}.

Physical meaning. In each discrete f_q-iteration:

  • The Reeb flow advances the fibre phase by \hbar_q (temporal information: one tick of the internal clock).
  • The q-connection correlates the current fibre with adjacent fibres at coupling q^{-1} (spatial information: one step of horizontal propagation).

A measurement within the light cone compares these two rates. The speed of light is how many fibres of spatial information are correlated per unit of Reeb phase advance:

  c_q =  \frac{\text{spatial coupling per step}}
                   {\text{temporal advance per step}}
  =  \frac{q^{-1}}{\hbar_q}
  =  \frac{1}{q - 1}.

Regime behaviour.

Regime q c_q = 1/(q-1) Interpretation
Deep-quantum q \to \infty \to 0 No spatial propagation; each fibre is isolated
Deep quantum \varphi^2 \approx 2.618 \approx 0.618 = 1/\varphi Sub-luminal; spatial coupling suppressed
Our universe q_0 \approx 9.093 {\sim}9 fibres correlated per Reeb phase advance
Near-classical 1.01 100 Fast spatial propagation; nearly continuous
Classical limit q \to 1^+ \to \infty Instantaneous spatial coupling; the q-connection reduces to A

At q = q_0, the speed of light is c \approx 9.093 in units where one Reeb phase advance = 1. This is not 1. The value c = 1 arises only if one redefines length units so that one "Planck length" equals c_q Reeb phases --- but that obscures the physics. In the natural units of the q-connection (where temporal ticks and spatial couplings are measured on the same footing), c is q-dependent and equals 1/(q-1).

Consistency: c diverges at the classical limit. As q \to 1, the q-connection A_q \to A (the full instanton connection): the horizontal component dominates, spatial correlations propagate instantly relative to the Reeb tick, and smooth Riemannian geometry with c = \infty (instantaneous spatial coupling) emerges. This is the Newtonian limit. To recover finite c in SI units, one rescales by the Planck time t_P^{\mathrm{SI}} = \sqrt{\hbar G / c_{\mathrm{SI}}^5}, which absorbs the divergence into the ratio of human-scale seconds to Reeb ticks.

Connection to the contact affine chart. The light cone of an affine chart (light cone) is the locus |Z| = c_q: the boundary where horizontal diffusion exactly matches vertical advance. Inside the cone (|Z| < c_q), spatial signals arrive within one Reeb circuit. Outside (|Z| > c_q), the signal requires multiple Reeb circuits and is causally delayed.

Lieb--Robinson bound. The locality of \nabla_q (it acts on adjacent fibres only) and the unitarity of the R-matrix (norm-preserving braiding in the rigid monoidal category \mathbf{C}) give an exponential decay outside the causal cone:

  \bigl\lVert
    [\mathcal{O}_x(n), \mathcal{O}_y(0)]
  \bigr\rVert
   \leq 
  C  e^{-\mu(d(x,y) -  n \cdot c_q \cdot \hbar_q)}

for constants C, \mu > 0 depending on q. The causal cone boundary is d(x,y) = n \cdot c_q \cdot \hbar_q = n \cdot q^{-1}: after n discrete steps, a signal has propagated n \cdot q^{-1} units of base-manifold distance.

Comparison with information-theoretic speed limits.

Result Bound QOU analog
Margolus--Levitin (1998) \leq 2E/\pi\hbar ops/sec n_R(q) = 1/\hbar_q ops per Planck time
Bremermann (1962) \leq mc^2/h bits/sec/kg \mathfrak{B}(q) = q\eta_q / (q-1)^2 bits per Planck time
Bekenstein (1981) S \leq 2\pi RE / \hbar c Fibre entropy \leq \eta_q per operation
Pawlowski (2009) No-signaling from information causality Lieb--Robinson decay outside \lvert Z\rvert = c_q cone
